items.question: In 2025 the Government of India announced that the next Census would include caste enumeration. When was caste last enumerated in a Census in India?
items.explanation: Caste was last enumerated in the Census of 1931 under British rule. Caste data was collected in 1941 but never published because of the Second World War, and from 1951 onwards only Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes have been counted, so 1921, 1951 and 1961 are incorrect.

items.question: Which film won the Best Feature Film award at the 71st National Film Awards announced in 2025?
options: 12th Fail
Jawan
Animal
Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway
Pathaan
items.explanation: 12th Fail won the Best Feature Film award at the 71st National Film Awards announced in 2025. Jawan won Shah Rukh Khan the Best Actor award, Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway won Rani Mukerji the Best Actress award, and Animal and Pathaan did not win the Best Feature Film award.

items.question: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, passed in August 2025, did which of the following?
options: Legalised all real-money online games
Banned real-money online gaming
Imposed a 50 percent tax on online games
Created a national esports league
Allowed online betting with licences
items.explanation: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 banned the offering and playing of real-money online games, while promoting esports and social games. It did not legalise real-money games, impose a 50 percent tax, create a national league, or license online betting.

items.question: Which vitamin is produced in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
options: Vitamin A
Vitamin B12
Vitamin D
Vitamin C
Vitamin E
items.explanation: Vitamin D is produced in the skin when ultraviolet sunlight converts 7-dehydrocholesterol into the vitamin. Vitamin A comes from foods such as carrots and liver, Vitamin B12 from animal foods, Vitamin C from citrus fruits, and Vitamin E from vegetable oils and nuts.

items.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 in response to which of the following?
options: The Partition of Bengal
The Simon Commission
The Quit India resolution
The Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
The Cabinet Mission plan
items.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in August 1920 after the Rowlatt Act of 1919, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 and the Khilafat issue. The Partition of Bengal in 1905 led to the Swadeshi Movement, the Simon Commission arrived in 1928, the Quit India resolution came in 1942, and the Cabinet Mission plan in 1946.

items.question: The Sanchi Stupa, one of the oldest stone structures in India, was originally commissioned by which ruler?
options: Chandragupta Maurya
Harshavardhana
Kanishka
Samudragupta
Ashoka
items.explanation: The Sanchi Stupa in Madhya Pradesh was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire, Harshavardhana ruled in the 7th century CE, Kanishka was a Kushana ruler, and Samudragupta was a Gupta emperor.

items.question: Match the books with their authors: 1. The White Tiger 2. Interpreter of Maladies 3. A Suitable Boy 4. The Argumentative Indian. Authors: A. Jhumpa Lahiri B. Amartya Sen C. Aravind Adiga D. Vikram Seth.
items.explanation: The correct pairing is The White Tiger with Aravind Adiga, Interpreter of Maladies with Jhumpa Lahiri, A Suitable Boy with Vikram Seth, and The Argumentative Indian with Amartya Sen. The White Tiger won the Booker Prize in 2008 and Interpreter of Maladies won the Pulitzer Prize in 2000.

items.question: Arrange the following constitutional developments in chronological order: A. Adoption of the Constitution B. First Amendment C. 42nd Amendment D. 73rd Amendment.
options: B, A, C, D
A, B, C, D
A, C, B, D
A, B, D, C
B, C, A, D
items.explanation: The correct order is the adoption of the Constitution in 1949, the First Amendment in 1951, the 42nd Amendment in 1976, and the 73rd Amendment in 1992. The Constitution had to be adopted before it could be amended, and the 42nd Amendment came long before the Panchayati Raj amendment of 1992.

items.question: Which of the following is NOT a classical dance form of India?
options: Bharatanatyam
Kathak
Bhangra
Odissi
Kuchipudi
items.explanation: Bhangra is not a classical dance form; it is a folk dance of Punjab. Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi and Kuchipudi are all among the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

items.question: What links M.S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug?
options: Both won the Nobel Peace Prize
Both were Prime Ministers of India
Both founded the Indian Council of Agricultural Research
Both led the Green Revolution in India
Both won the Bharat Ratna
items.explanation: Both men led the Green Revolution: Norman Borlaug developed high-yielding wheat varieties, and M.S. Swaminathan adapted them in India. Only Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970, neither was a Prime Minister, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research was founded in 1929, and only Swaminathan received the Bharat Ratna in 2024.

items.question: The headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) is located in which city?
options: New Delhi
Dhaka
Colombo
Islamabad
Kathmandu
items.explanation: SAARC is headquartered in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal. New Delhi, Dhaka, Colombo and Islamabad are the capitals of other SAARC member countries but do not host the organisation's secretariat.
